extracted.intended_audience: Thomson Reuters employees, management, trustees, and external stakeholders (news consumers, subscribers, and regulators)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal statement of the Trust Principles that govern Thomson Reuters’ journalistic and corporate conduct, specifying standards of integrity, independence, impartiality, and the governance safeguards that protect them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to act with integrity, independence and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Principles impose obligations on the company and its employees to act at all times with integrity, independence and freedom from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These obligations are described as fundamental to the entire business of Thomson Reuters and date from 1941; they form the overarching standard that guides all company activities and journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: No concentration of control by any one interest
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group or faction;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle guards against takeover or control by a single interest that could compromise independence; historically enforced via special governance structures (see Founders Share Company).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of integrity, independence and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: That the integrity, independence and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit, continuous obligation for the organisation to maintain impartiality in its reporting and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply unbiased and reliable news services
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall supply unbiased and reliable news services to newspapers, news agencies, broadcasters and other media subscribers and to businesses, governments, institutions, individuals and others with whom Thomson Reuters has or may have contracts;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the audience scope (media, businesses, governments, institutions, individuals) and ties reliability and lack of bias to the company’s service obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay due regard to the many interests served (beyond the media)
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall pay due regard to the many interests which it serves in addition to those of the media;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires balancing or considering the legitimate interests of a broad range of stakeholders, not prioritising media customers alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous effort to develop and adapt services to maintain leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: That no effort shall be spared to expand, develop and adapt the news and other services and products of Thomson Reuters so as to maintain its leading position in the international news and information business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates active innovation and service improvement to preserve the organisation’s international leadership while operating under the Trust Principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance safeguard: Founders Share Company and single golden share
rubrics_metrics.description: A unique structure (the Reuters Founders Share Company) holding a single, golden Founder Share was created to safeguard the Trust Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the institutional mechanism used since 1984 to protect independence (trustees holding a Founder Share empowered to defend the principles); includes historical context about its role during mergers and takeovers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement by major shareholders and companies to adopt and uphold the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Thomson, Reuters and Woodbridge (the controlling shareholder) agreed to adopt and uphold the Trust Principles and to implement certain changes to charter documents and company structure to support them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes contractual and charter-level commitments by owners and the company to embed the Trust Principles into governance and corporate documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directors’ duty to have due regard to the Trust Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The charter documents require Thomson Reuters directors, in the performance of their duties, to have due regard to the Reuters Trust Principles, by the proper exercise of their powers and in accordance with their other duties as directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a formal duty on board members to consider and observe the Trust Principles when making decisions, linking the Principles to fiduciary and statutory duties.
